text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.3% today as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East intensified once again. After a brief dip on Oct 20 when diplomacy seemed possible, the stock has now declined for three straight days following reports that the U.S. is withdrawing diplomats from Saudi Arabia and preparing to resume strikes against Iran. While higher oil prices (Brent at $112+) typically help refiners by boosting fuel margins, the immediate uncertainty and risk of regional conflict disrupting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz is weighing on the sector today.

The backdrop here is real tension: diesel prices have already spiked from Ukraine's strikes on Russian supply, and now potential Iranian retaliation or U.S. strikes threaten to further destabilize crude flows. At the same time, U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity with healthy product inventories (gasoline, diesel), so the refiner isn't supply-constrained—but geopolitical shock risk is what's driving sentiment lower right now.
